It was held concurrently with the [[2024 United States presidential election]], [[2024 United States Senate elections|other elections]] to the U.S. Senate, [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]], and various state and local elections. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] congresswoman [[Elissa Slotkin]] won her first term in office, narrowly defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former congressman [[Mike Rogers (Michigan politician)|Mike Rogers]]. She succeeded Democratic incumbent [[Debbie Stabenow]], who did not seek a fifth term.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=January 5, 2023 |title=Sen. Stabenow will not seek re-election in 2024 |url=https://www.uppermichiganssource.com/2023/01/05/sen-stabenow-will-not-seek-re-election-2024/ |access-date=January 5, 2023 |website=Upper Michigan Source |publisher=TV6 News Team |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Siobhan |date=January 5, 2023 |title=Democratic Sen. Debbie Stabenow Won't Seek Re-Election |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/democratic-sen-debbie-stabenow-wont-seek-re-election-11672930938 |access-date=January 5, 2023 |website=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US}} Primary elections took place on August 6, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Slotkin won the Democratic nomination with 76% of the vote over actor [[Hill Harper]], and Rogers won the Republican nomination with 63% of the vote over former congressman [[Justin Amash]]. As Republican presidential nominee [[Donald Trump]] carried Michigan on the same ballot, this was the first time Michigan voted for candidates of different political parties for U.S. senator and president since Democrat [[Donald Riegle|Don Riegle]] was [[1988 United States Senate election in Michigan|re-elected]] as Republican [[George H. W. Bush]] carried the state in [[1988 United States presidential election|1988]]. On November 6, 2024, major news organizations projected that Slotkin had won the election.{{cite web |last1=Slodysko |first1=Brian |title=Why AP called the Michigan Senate race for Elissa Slotkin |url=https://apnews.com/article/michigan-senate-race-call-explain-rogers-slotkin-3e6ae97face22dc1d5f4e86c2fd09736 |website=AP News |date=November 6, 2024 |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=6 November 2024}}{{cite web |last1=Aleem |first1=Zeeshan |title=Elissa Slotkin beats Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race, NBC News projects |url=https://www.msnbc.com/top-stories/latest/elissa-slotkin-wins-mike-rogers-michigan-senate-election-rcna174543 |website=MSNBC |date=November 6, 2024 |publisher=NBC |access-date=6 November 2024}}{{cite web |title=Democrat Elissa Slotkin will win Michigan Senate seat, CNN projects |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/06/politics/elissa-slotkin-michigan-senate-race/index.html |website=CNN |date=November 6, 2024 |access-date=6 November 2024}} Slotkin received 23,847 fewer votes than [[Kamala Harris]], while Rogers received 122,956 fewer votes than [[Donald Trump]]. {{TOC limit|3}} ==Background== Michigan is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple]] state. However, Democrats had seen much more success in recent years in the state.
